title: The seat timeout is a wall-clock cap from spawn, not a liveness test: a working seat is killed at MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS while its tool call runs
description:
Measured on UnAI 2026-09-18. `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts` arms `setTimeout(beginTermination, timeoutMs)` at spawn (`MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 30 min, `wrapper-knobs.ts`). The "seat quiet: Nms since last output (…, Nms to timeout, … 0 bytes seen)" lines are notices only. The seat is `claude -p …` without `--output-format stream-json`, so it writes nothing until it finishes: every seat shows "0 bytes seen" for its whole life and the quiet timer can never distinguish a stuck seat from a busy one.

Live: nodes 3 and 4 took 15-20 min and finished; node 5 (15f56b77) was at minute 26 with a live `bash.exe` tool child started 60 s earlier (claude.exe cpu 25 s, 33 threads) and was on course to be killed at minute 30 mid-work, then re-spawned to repeat the same 30-minute race. The owner raised the cap to 60 min in the product's launcher (UnAI `.moe-next/start.ps1` 19733cb) as a stopgap.

Make liveness real:
1. Launch the seat with streaming output (`--output-format stream-json --verbose` for claude; codex equivalent) or observe tool children of the seat (a live child process under the seat's pid, or CPU delta since the last check) and treat that as "output seen"; the quiet notice must then mean what it says.
2. Kill on SILENCE (no output, no live tool child, no CPU progress for `quiet` ms), keep a much larger absolute cap (e.g. 3 h) as the backstop, and name which one fired in the log ("killed: silent 20 min" vs "killed: absolute cap 3 h").
3. The wrapper log line for a kill must say what the seat was doing (last tool child command, if any) so a kill is attributable.
definitionOfDone: A seat that produces no stdout but has a live tool child or CPU progress is NOT killed at the silence threshold; a seat with none of those is; an arm pins each with a fake child/probe.
The absolute cap is a separate, larger knob (name it) and the kill log line names which limit fired and the seat's last observed activity.
Claude seats stream (or the equivalent liveness probe is wired) so `bytes seen` is non-zero during a normal run; a wrapper-entrypoint or spawner arm covers the launch args.
wrapper-knobs.ts and its CLAUDE.md/README knob table document both knobs; PROJECT_STACK_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS carries any new MOE_* knob (roster test updated).

(b) Confirm task-8bc14883 is DONE and read how it left `windows-project-stack-boundary.ts` and `docs/agent-stack-runbook.md`, since both are edited again here. (c) Measure the real process tree of a seat on this host — start any long-lived child through `cmd.exe` the way agent-spawner.ts does with `shell: true`, and dump its tree with the leaf's own probe — so you know which pid the spawner hands the probe and that the leaf's 'strictly below the provider process' rule matches reality. (d) `wc -l apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts`: record both as the baseline for step 4's net-negative requirement.

RED FIRST — the knob and the bearer TTL. In apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/wrapper-knobs.test.ts add failing arms: (1) `readWrapperKnobs({})` yields `agentMaxRuntimeMs` 10_800_000; (2) `MOE_AGENT_MAX_RUNTIME_MS: "abc"` and `"0"` refuse with the exact code WRAPPER_ENV_INVALID naming that variable, mirroring the existing MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS arms at :49-51; (3) a max runtime SMALLER than the silence window — e.g. `MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS: "7200000", MOE_AGENT_MAX_RUNTIME_MS: "3600000"` — refuses with WRAPPER_ENV_INVALID naming BOTH variables, because the silence kill could otherwise never be reached; (4) THE LOAD-BEARING ONE: `sessionTtlMs` now derives from the ABSOLUTE CAP, `Math.max(CLAIM_TTL_MS, agentMaxRuntimeMs) + SESSION_EXIT_GRACE_MS`, not from the silence window. RE-AIM the three existing pins that encode the old derivation — :14 (the default fixture `THIRTY_MINUTES_MS + 60_000`), :40 (`7_200_000 + 60_000`) and :44 — never delete them: each now asserts the cap-derived value, and one arm must set a LONG silence window with a default cap to show the TTL follows the cap, not the window. State in a comment on that arm why: a bearer still derived from the silence window expires mid-run on a seat the cap allows to keep working, so it survives the kill and then cannot review_submit or work_release. Run the file and CONFIRM RED before step 3; quote the failures.

GREEN — the knob. In apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/wrapper-knobs.ts add `MOE_AGENT_MAX_RUNTIME_MS` via the existing `integer(...)` helper (minimum 1, default 10_800_000 declared as a named constant beside DEFAULT_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS), expose it on the returned knobs as `agentMaxRuntimeMs`, refuse by name with WRAPPER_ENV_INVALID when it is below `agentTimeoutMs`, and change `sessionTtlMs` to derive from `agentMaxRuntimeMs`. Update the file's comment at :66-68 and the doc comment of `agentTimeoutMs`: MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS is now the SILENCE window — how long a seat may go with positively observed inactivity — and MOE_AGENT_MAX_RUNTIME_MS is the absolute lifetime from which the bearer TTL follows. Keep the division of labour stated there: this file refuses loudly, the spawner reads leniently. Confirm every arm from step 2 is GREEN, including the three re-aimed pins.

Replace the wall clock with the leaf's liveness tracker — as a SWAP, keeping the spawner net-negative. (a) apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawn-contract.ts: add ONE optional field `maxRuntimeMs?: number` to `AgentSpawnerOptions` beside `timeoutMs?` (that file is 403 lines and over the cap already; one line, and its split stays the follow-up task-4444d180 recorded). (b) apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.ts: resolve `maxRuntimeMs` exactly as `timeoutMs` is resolved at :67-69 — `options.maxRuntimeMs ?? lenient read of MOE_AGENT_MAX_RUNTIME_MS ?? default` — so both readers agree. Delete the one-shot `setTimeout` at :399-402. Build one `createSeatLivenessTracker({ startedAtMs, silenceMs: timeoutMs, maxRuntimeMs })` per seat; call `noteOutput(now())` wherever output already updates `lastOutputAt` (:247-251); on the EXISTING `quietNoticeMs` interval (:404-414) call the probe with the pid the spawner holds, feed the result to `noteSample`, and read `verdict(now())`. On KILL_SILENT or KILL_ABSOLUTE_CAP call the existing `beginTermination()` and log ONE line naming which limit fired and the verdict's `lastActivity`, e.g. `killed: silent <N> min (last activity: <command>)` versus `killed: absolute cap <N> h (...)`. The quiet notice must stop computing 'to timeout' from `startedAt` — it now reports the silence window remaining and the last activity. Inject the probe through a new optional spawner option defaulting to `createWindowsSeatProbe()` on win32 and to a probe returning UNKNOWN elsewhere, so tests supply a fake and a platform with no probe gets only the absolute cap. Clear the interval on every exit path exactly as `quietTimer` is cleared today; a leaked interval keeps the process alive and probes a dead pid forever. `wc -l` both files and confirm agent-spawner.ts came out at or below step 1's baseline.

Pin the wiring in apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.test.ts with an injected fake probe and the existing injected clock (the file already injects `now` so the quiet notice is testable without waiting a real minute — reuse that harness). DoD 1, one arm per case, each asserting by VALUE: (1) no output, the fake probe reporting a live tool child, past the silence window — the seat is NOT terminated; (2) no output, no tool child, CPU rising — NOT terminated; (3) no output, OBSERVED with no tool child and flat CPU, past the window — terminated, and the kill line names the SILENT limit with its minutes; (4) the probe returning only UNKNOWN past the silence window — NOT terminated, then past the absolute cap — terminated with the kill line naming the ABSOLUTE CAP. Arm (4) is the one that proves an unobservable seat is never killed for silence; do not let it pass on a probe that silently returns OBSERVED. DoD 3: an arm asserts that on win32 the spawner's default probe is the leaf's Windows probe and that the probe is actually called on the interval with the spawned pid — so 'liveness is wired' is a tested fact, not a comment. Assert the interval is cleared after exit (no further probe calls). MUTATION-VERIFY arm (4): back up agent-spawner.ts to %TEMP%/moe-task-8f653d86-agent-spawner-<workerId>.ts recording its SHA256 (task id in the path, because seat ids are reused and a seat-only backup can hold the wrong vintage), make the spawner treat UNKNOWN as silence, confirm arm (4) goes RED and quote the line, restore by copying the backup back — never `git checkout --` on this shared tree — and prove the restore by SHA256 equality in a call SEPARATE from the restore.

Carry the knob to every process that enforces it (DoD 4 roster clause). (a) apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper-main.ts: pass `maxRuntimeMs: knobs.agentMaxRuntimeMs` beside `timeoutMs: knobs.agentTimeoutMs` at :405, and rewrite the doc comment at :76-82, which currently calls MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS 'the hard lifetime of one agent process, from which the agent's bearer TTL is derived' — false after this row. It must say MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS is the silence window and MOE_AGENT_MAX_RUNTIME_MS the absolute lifetime the bearer TTL follows. (b) packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-project-stack-boundary.ts: add `"MOE_AGENT_MAX_RUNTIME_MS"` to PROJECT_STACK_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS beside `"MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS"` (:45). Without it `moe start` silently drops the variable — the operator sets it and nothing that enforces it ever sees it. (c) packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-project-stack-boundary.test.ts:222-226 pins that roster with `toEqual`; add the key there in the same position. Before staging either runner file run `git diff HEAD -- <file>` and stage only your own hunk: task-8bc14883 edited this same file for the launcher argv, and whole-file staging in this shared checkout sweeps a peer's uncommitted hunk into your commit. Then run the runner package's tests — resolve its name from packages/runner/package.json first, because a wrong `--filter` prints 'No projects matched the filters' and exits 0 — and quote the count line.

Document both knobs where operators and agents read them (DoD 4). apps/daemon/CLAUDE.md (:69 names MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS among the wrapper knobs) and docs/agent-stack-runbook.md both list the MOE_WRAPPER_* knobs; those two are the knob tables DoD 4 means — there is no separate README table. In each, state in the surrounding register: MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS (default 30 min) is how long a seat may go with POSITIVELY OBSERVED inactivity — no output, no tool child, no CPU progress — before it is stopped; MOE_AGENT_MAX_RUNTIME_MS (default 3 h) is the absolute backstop, from which the seat's bearer TTL follows; a seat whose activity cannot be observed on the platform is stopped only by the absolute cap; and the wrapper log line for a kill names which limit fired and what the seat was last doing. An operator who had raised MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS as a stopgap (as the owner did in UnAI's start.ps1) should learn from these lines that their setting now means silence, and that busy seats are no longer killed by it. docs/agent-stack-runbook.md was also edited by task-8bc14883; `git diff HEAD -- docs/agent-stack-runbook.md` and stage only your own hunk.

GATES AND ADVERSARIAL REVIEW. (A) `pnpm typecheck`, projects counted; the daemon project carries erasableSyntaxOnly, so anything added must be erasable. (B) `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon exec vitest run --root . --config package.json src/orchestrator/agent-spawner.test.ts src/orchestrator/wrapper-knobs.test.ts src/orchestrator/seat-liveness.test.ts`, count line quoted — read the OUTPUT, not the exit code. (C) The full `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and the runner package's tests, both count lines quoted; the root lane covers no apps/** file, so a bare root count proves nothing here. (D) Attribute any red by the path-attributed baseline rule; the full daemon suite throws spurious 5s-timeout reds under parallelism, so re-run a failing file ALONE before attributing it, name which you re-ran, and capture stderr. (E) ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, in the completion record: Can a seat still be killed while its tool call runs — walk the exact tree measured in step 1 through the tracker. What happens if the probe hangs rather than failing — does the interval stack up overlapping probe calls, and does a slow probe delay a due absolute-cap kill? Is the interval cleared on every exit path, including a spawn failure and a kill during a probe? Is a seat with a PERSISTENT helper child (an MCP server process, say) now unkillable for silence — and does the absolute cap still bound it? Does the bearer TTL now cover the longest a seat can live, and is the claim renewable for that whole time? What does a Windows host WITHOUT PowerShell or CIM do — UNKNOWN, and therefore cap-only? Is the ~3 h scoped bearer an acceptable exposure, and is that stated? (F) Record as follow-up comments on this row, not new rows: splitting agent-spawner.ts (480) and agent-spawn-contract.ts (403) below 400 lines; a POSIX probe, so a stuck seat there is killed for silence rather than at the cap; and the e2e harness tests/e2e/foundation/j1-loop-harness.ts:342, which sets MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS as if it were a wall clock and may now mean something different to that test.

reopenReason: Governor backlog triage 2026-09-18, owner-directed. RE-MEASURED LIVE at origin/main: agent-spawner.ts:399-402 arms `setTimeout(kill, timeoutMs)` at spawn and never rearms it; `lastOutputAt` exists only to drive the quiet NOTICE at :405-414, which prints "Nms to timeout" computed from startedAt. So a seat producing output continuously is still killed at MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS. The defect is real and unfixed. It is the most expensive one left on the board: it kills productive seats mid-round on the owner's live UnAI build, which is exactly where 30-minute rounds live. Architect: re-measure before planning, and treat "is the cap a liveness test or a wall clock" as the DoD's centre.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
RE-MEASURED AT HEAD 2026-09-18. The governor's reopen reason is accurate. The fix was split because it measured 11 files against the 10-file cap: this row is the CONSUMER, and the pure decider + probe live in the LEAF task-eca3780de7bb44f09ebe669a568bcbda, whose description pins the exact exported contract this plan wires. dependsOn is [task-eca3780d, task-8bc14883] — see insight 9 for why the second one is a safety ordering.

(1) THE DEFECT. `agent-spawner.ts:399-402`: `timer = setTimeout(() => { log(`... agent exceeded ${timeoutMs}ms; killing`); beginTermination(); }, timeoutMs);` — armed ONCE at spawn, never rearmed. It is a wall clock, not a liveness test. `:404-414` is a notice only; it prints "Nms to timeout" computed from `startedAt`, not from any activity.

(2) WHY OUTPUT CANNOT BE THE SIGNAL. The seat is `claude -p` without `--output-format` (`:154`), which writes nothing until it finishes, so every seat reports "0 bytes seen" its whole life. Streaming was REJECTED for the reason recorded on the leaf: `seat-exit-classifier.ts` pattern-matches the seat's TEXT to detect provider limits, with regexes measured against specific claude.exe builds, and its own comment at :58 warns a seat printing "rate limit" inside its JSON output must NOT park the provider. The leaf's process probe changes no output format.

(3) THE SPAWNER IS ALREADY OVER THE LINE CAP. `agent-spawner.ts` is 480 lines, past the 400 split line BEFORE this row. The leaf owns ALL liveness state (`createSeatLivenessTracker`) precisely so this row's spawner diff is a SWAP, not an addition: the wall-clock `setTimeout` and the notice's startedAt arithmetic come out, a probe interval and one tracker call go in. The spawner must come out NET-NEGATIVE or net-zero in lines; a proper split below 400 is a follow-up comment, not this row.

(4) THE KNOB IS READ TWICE, DELIBERATELY. `wrapper-knobs.ts:69` validates `MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS` loudly via `integer(...)` and refuses a bad value with `WRAPPER_ENV_INVALID`; `agent-spawner.ts:67-69` then reads the SAME variable leniently (`Number(process.env[...])`, falling back on anything non-positive). The comment at wrapper-knobs.ts:66-68 states that division of labour on purpose (refused by name HERE, before the spawner ever reads it). The new absolute-cap knob must follow the SAME two-reader pattern, and the two readers must agree on meaning.

(5) THE HIDDEN CONSUMER THAT WOULD HAVE BROKEN THE FIX: THE BEARER TTL. `wrapper-knobs.ts:79` — `sessionTtlMs: Math.max(CLAIM_TTL_MS, agentTimeoutMs) + SESSION_EXIT_GRACE_MS` — and `agent-wrapper-main.ts:79` says outright that MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS is "the hard lifetime of one agent process, from which the agent's bearer TTL is derived". Constants at wrapper-knobs.ts:37-44: DEFAULT_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS 30 min, CLAIM_TTL_MS 30 min, SESSION_EXIT_GRACE_MS 60 s. So today a seat's MCP bearer dies at ~31 min. Once a busy seat may live to the absolute cap, a bearer still derived from the silence threshold EXPIRES MID-RUN: the seat survives the kill and then cannot `review_submit` or `work_release` at the end — worse than being killed, because it burns the tokens first. `sessionTtlMs` MUST derive from the ABSOLUTE CAP. It is consumed at `agent-wrapper-main.ts:305` and pinned at `wrapper-knobs.test.ts:14`, `:40` (`7_200_000 + 60_000`) and `:44`.

(6) THE WORK CLAIM FOLLOWS FROM THE BEARER. `agent-wrapper.ts:176` sets the claim `expiresAt = now + claimTtlMs` (30 min, constant, not derived). The wrapper does NOT renew it; the SEAT does, via `work_renew` — the mission text tells it to at `agent-mission-text.ts:103` and `:345`. `work_renew` needs a live bearer, so fixing insight 5 is what keeps long seats' claims alive; without it an expired bearer lets the claim lapse and the item is double-staffed.

(7) THE SPAWNER OPTIONS TYPE lives in `agent-spawn-contract.ts` (`AgentSpawnerOptions` from :20; `timeoutMs?`, `quietNoticeMs?`, `killGraceMs?`). The absolute cap needs one new optional field there for test injection, mirroring `timeoutMs`. That file is 403 lines, also over the cap, and is being edited by task-4444d180 (its error class at :72-81) — one added line, flagged, split deferred as that row already recorded.

(8) THE ENV ROSTER. `packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-project-stack-boundary.ts:41-45` — `PROJECT_STACK_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS` lists `"MOE_AGENT_TIMEOUT_MS"`; its test `windows-project-stack-boundary.test.ts:222-226` pins the FULL list with `toEqual`. `moe start` forwards ONLY allowlisted keys to the stack and on to the wrapper, so a new MOE_* knob missing from this roster is silently dropped: the operator sets it and nothing that enforces it ever sees it. Exported via @moe/runner (index.ts:285), consumed at project-launch-environment.ts:6 and project-manager-launch.ts:105/:114.
